trust_decision.summary: createConnection decides whether a literal-IP host may be connected by running validateIPAddress({address: host}) before delegating to super.createConnection; the denial is currently delivered as a synchronous throw, so the decision surfaces as an exception out of http.get/https.get instead of an 'error' event.

landing_point.why: The advisory names createConnection() and a literal private-IP host; the first synchronous `throw validationError` inside a createConnection override is here in RequestFilteringHttpAgent, which is what http.get/http.request reaches.

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helper used by both agents' createConnection (no direct public entry point)
RequestFilteringHttpAgent#createConnection, reached through http.request/http.get, globalHttpAgent and useAgent()
RequestFilteringHttpsAgent#createConnection, reached through https.request/https.get, globalHttpsAgent and useAgent()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report's repro is an http.get to a literal IPv4, so the HTTPS agent can be argued to be a separate exported class / separate feature, even though its createConnection is a line-for-line copy of the HTTP one.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The allow path must keep letting literal private-IP hosts connect: allowIPAddressList is preferred over the private-range check and returns before any error, and allowPrivateIPAddress: true does the same. An over-broad fix that rejects every literal-IP host in createConnection, or that emits a bare socket error without the original 'It is private IP address' message, breaks both the allowed connection and the error-message contract asserted by the existing tests.

O6_input_shapes: literal IPv4 address in options.host with a connectionListener supplied (http.get / https.get path)
the same literal-IP host on the HTTPS agent's createConnection (second implementation)
no connectionListener supplied by a direct caller of the public createConnection method (helper takes the socket.destroy(error) branch)
non-literal hostname that goes through the DNS lookup path (makeLookup callback already delivers the error asynchronously)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A pre-flight validation inside useAgent() that rejects a URL whose host is a literal private IP before an agent is chosen
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: useAgent is the documented entry point and a maintainer could reasonably add early URL validation there for a clearer error; it would throw synchronously from the same guard, reproducing the crash one layer up.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A createSocket/createConnection wrapper that validates the literal host inside the lookup half of the check (makeLookup) and returns an error socket from there
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: makeLookup is already the place where the DNS-resolved address is validated and its errors are callback-delivered, so a maintainer adding deny-list handling there could easily mirror the same denial path with a synchronous throw.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third agent class (proxy, http2 or legacy transport) added next to the two existing agents and copying their createConnection body
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RequestFilteringHttpsAgent is itself a copy of RequestFilteringHttpAgent, so copying the createConnection override into one more transport class is the maintainer's established pattern.

O9_family: Uncaught exception / synchronous throw from an agent's createConnection instead of asynchronous error delivery (CWE-248), crashing the host process

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm 10.15.0; tsc -p . for build, tsc --noEmit for typecheck; tsx --test to run node:test
O10_build.project_tests: test/request-filtering-agent.test.ts (node:test via tsx, ~13 cases: allow/deny lists, CIDR, meta IP, IPv6 literals, DNS-lookup and redirect paths). Two pre-existing cases reach the internet (example.com at test/request-filtering-agent.test.ts:344, bit.ly at :297); the private-IP rejection cases and the fix's added cases do not, because validation runs before any connect.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the http.get(...) call in try/catch at the application layer, or replace only the HTTP agent's `throw validationError` with a plain socket.destroy(); that stops the crash in the reported example but leaves the HTTPS agent throwing and drops the validation message from the emitted error.
